clue.text: Assist fools in novel all about islander

indicators.note: all about says the whole assembled string is turned round end to end
in says the helper and the fools go inside the novel word

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new
to assist is to aid
nits are fools or idiots in British slang

explanation.surface: A novel about an island native in which someone helps some idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all about' turns the whole assembled string round, so it reads backwards; 'novel' is the adjective, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Caribbean islands is an islander by birth.

clue.text: Buzzer got played quietly

parts.note: got as a passive auxiliary ('it got stolen') stands for was
p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A doorbell or game-show buzzer sounded softly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'got played quietly' as 'was p': 'got' swaps for 'was' in a passive, and p is the musical mark for soft playing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinging insect that hums in flight is fancifully called a buzzer.

clue.text: Make effective use of spoon, gripping a shaft

indicators.note: gripping means the outer phrase holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to use a spoon effectively is to stir well

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to hold a spoon properly and use it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical opening running through a building for a staircase is a kind of shaft.

clue.text: Blowing up evidence set to keep real value

parts.note: blowing up, as of a balloon, is inflation
proof is evidence

explanation.surface: Evidence of a bombing, arranged to keep its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing up' looks like an explosion, but here it is filling with air, and the definition is economic.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment whose value is protected against rising prices keeps its real worth.

clue.text: I make an effort to support dull Russian man

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits below, so it comes after

parts.note: dim means dull, lacking brightness or wit
to try is to make an effort

explanation.surface: Someone striving to prop up a stupid Russian fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so 'to support' puts it after.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimitry is a common Russian given name for a male.

clue.text: Close second, after one in Rhone city

indicators.note: after puts the second piece at the end of what precedes
in says the numeral goes inside the city name

parts.note: Arles is a city on the river Rhone in southern France
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Finishing a close second, behind someone in a French city race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' is the adjective meaning stuffy, not a verb or a near-miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that is stuffy and oppressive, with no breeze, is described as close.

clue.text: On a lake, this wader would provide proofs of whereabouts

indicators.note: would provide says this word, with the extra letters set on it, makes the longer word, so those letters are removed from it

parts.note: alibis prove someone was elsewhere

explanation.surface: A bird standing on a lake somehow supplies alibis.
explanation.walkthrough: Put A and L in front of the wader and you get ALIBIS; the parse runs that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: It may be smoked cheese, right?

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: Asking whether some cheese can be smoked.
explanation.walkthrough: Smoked cheese is a real thing, but the definition is a pipe made of brier root.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe carved from heath root is called a brier and is smoked.

clue.text: Son, little mischief-maker to visit king and queen, is perhaps number one fan

parts.note: an elf is a small mischievous sprite
to see someone can mean to visit them
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A naughty child calls on royalty and turns out to be their biggest fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' is oneself, so a fan of number one cares only for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to their own interests above all is a fan of themselves, looking after number one.

clue.text: Not oneself when missing letter?

definitions.meaning: behaving unusually, unlike one's normal personality
lacking a single letter, a character, of the alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: Acting unlike one's usual self is uncharacteristic, and a character is also a written symbol.

clue.text: Noisy argument over losing a bit of football memorabilia?

indicators.note: losing means the next letter is taken away
over means the word for the argument is turned backwards

parts.note: a fracas is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A row among supporters ends with someone losing a souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns FRACAS into SACARF; 'losing a' drops one A.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters wear a knitted strip in team colours, a classic souvenir of the game.

clue.text: Animal god aloft, one completely lacking tail

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war
aloft means up in the air
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: lacking tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means completely

explanation.surface: A creature or deity in the sky that has no tail at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo or koala, with a pouch for its young, is a kind of mammal, so an animal.

clue.text: Do Bard's theatre, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of these words may be arranged differently

parts.note: here the S of the possessive is kept as a letter

explanation.surface: An invitation to stage Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare; the whole clue both supplies the letters and describes acting on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing Shakespeare means acting on stage, the idiom for a stage career.

clue.text: Leaves when due to be thrown out?

definitions.text: Leaves when due to be thrown out?

parts.words: Leaves when due to be thrown out?
parts.note: leaves suggests autumn foliage, but here means sheets of paper headed for the bin

explanation.definitionFit: Discarded sheets of paper, leaves of a book or pad, go in the bin.

clue.text: Any time, anyhow: that's convenience

indicators.note: anyhow means in any order at all, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that something available at any hour is handy.
explanation.definitionFit: A useful facility, like a nearby shop or pool, is a convenience.

clue.text: Goon's search interrupting watch

indicators.note: interrupting means the search word breaks into the watch word

parts.note: to watch is to see
to comb is to search thoroughly

explanation.surface: A fool's hunt is interrupted while someone keeps watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Secombe was one of the Goons, the 1950s BBC radio comedy team; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Secombe performed in The Goon Show, the BBC radio comedy, alongside Milligan and Sellers.

clue.text: Twisted elm carried around university home for Victorians

indicators.note: twisted means the tree's letters are wrung into another order
around means the carried word surrounds the university letter

parts.note: borne means carried

explanation.surface: A gnarled tree trunk moved around a college campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorians' are people of Victoria, the Australian state, not the 19th century; ELM twisted gives MEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Melbourne is the capital city of the state of Victoria in Australia.

clue.text: Daughter completes time away from people with nippers?

indicators.note: completes puts the daughter at the very end

parts.note: alone means apart from others

explanation.surface: A girl finishes a spell of solitude, away from her children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nippers' suggests children but means claws.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of prey have claws that grip and pinch, so they are equipped with nippers.

clue.text: Senior old boy in the German strip

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the German article

parts.note: die is a German word for the
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An elderly former pupil in a German football strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strip' looks like a kit worn, but it is the verb meaning undress.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off one's clothes, or a robe, is to undress or strip.

clue.text: Fool's daily deception

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day
a lie is a deception

explanation.surface: A newspaper fooling its readers every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is not a newspaper here but a char, a British cleaner; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a silly person, a fool or idiot.

clue.text: Sport sprain and so on, with the foot going first

indicators.note: the foot is the last letter, which here moves to the front

parts.note: a rick is a sprain or wrench
etc is the abbreviation for et cetera, and so on

explanation.surface: Sprains and similar injuries in sport, the foot taking the brunt.
explanation.walkthrough: RICK and ETC run together as RICKETC; the final C moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat-and-ball game played between teams of eleven is a sport.

clue.text: Artist in irregular cartoon strip is an off-putting person

indicators.note: in says the artist goes inside the jumbled letters
irregular says the letters of the strip words are disordered

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: An artist working on a patchy comic strip keeps delaying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-putting' means putting things off, not repellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually delays tasks keeps putting them off.

clue.text: Most of bowler's set hampers batting, affecting some in the field?

indicators.note: hampers says the shortened set holds the batting word inside
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricket over that hinders the batsman, troubling the fielders.
explanation.walkthrough: The field is a farmer's, not a cricket ground: sheep are in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to sheep, animals found in a field.

clue.text: Pardon bowler perhaps going after wickets

indicators.note: going after means the hat follows the wickets letter

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wickets
a bowler is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler chasing wickets asks to be excused.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the hat comes after, so below, W.
explanation.definitionFit: Said when one has not heard, 'Pardon?' and 'What?' are interchangeable requests to repeat.

clue.text: Number in river I drench, irritating climber

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy

indicators.note: in says the number goes inside the rest

parts.note: to drench is to soak

explanation.surface: Someone soaking a number in the river Po.
explanation.walkthrough: POISON IVY also fits the definition and crossings may tempt it, but the wordplay rules it out.
explanation.definitionFit: This American shrub, related to sumac, climbs and causes a skin rash.

clue.text: Light from Desert Orchid?

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the horse's name

explanation.surface: A glow coming from Desert Orchid, the famous grey racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert Orchid was a much-loved British racehorse of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable lamp, or British flashlight, is a light.

clue.text: Miasma's radius that's alarming

parts.note: eek is the cry when something alarms you

explanation.surface: A reaction of horror to the extent of a foul fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is an unpleasant smell or vapour, a stench.

clue.text: Gambler intended to report improved condition

parts.note: a better is one who bets

indicators.note: to report means the word is spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A gambler meaning to announce that things are looking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvement, a change for the better, is a state of being improved.
